original_test_intent: Validate both BMC SSH console resource controls: the maximum simultaneous session admission boundary and automatic closure of an idle authenticated session at the configured timeout, while preserving management access and unrelated sessions.
original_method: Select the unique row; identify BMC firmware/SSH daemon and authoritative MaxSess/SessTimeOut specification; use a dedicated account and independent recovery console; inventory existing SSH/process/session state; create uniquely marked controlled sessions sequentially/concurrently up to the approved boundary plus one; record handshake/auth/shell success or exact rejection; keep one accepted session idle with keepalives disabled according to policy and timestamp its server-initiated closure through the configured timeout/grace; ensure active control session remains available; close every test session and verify resource count/audit returns to baseline.
manual_activity: An operator supplies/approves the session-policy values, dedicated account, concurrency/timeout plan and recovery path; an agent may open, idle, observe and close only uniquely marked test sessions within that plan.
required_inputs: BMC firmware/SSH server build and authoritative MaxSess/SessTimeOut values
Scope of limit: per account, source IP, protocol, daemon or global; whether the control/recovery session counts
Expected rejection point/error, connection/auth/shell definition and race/settling tolerance
Idle definition, client/server keepalive configuration, timeout start/maximum/grace, dedicated test account and independent console/admin recovery
safety_requirements: Inventory and account for existing sessions without exposing other users
Preserve one independent recovery path that does not consume or depend on the tested limit
Open sessions only up to approved boundary plus one and rate-limit creation
Disable or account for keepalives/traffic in the timeout session while maintaining a separate active control session
Stop on BMC latency/resource errors/lockout; close only marked test sessions and never repeat automatically
agent_execution_scope: Create uniquely marked test sessions and record each handshake/auth/shell disposition
Measure one approved idle session's server-side timeout and correlate with audit/process/session data
Verify unrelated sessions and BMC responsiveness and perform complete test-session cleanup
Do not guess limits, saturate beyond boundary, expose credentials, close other users, retry lockout or decide verdict
engineer_actions: Approve both policy values and their per-account/global/protocol scope
Approve exact MaxSess admission/rejection and SessTimeOut idle/keepalive/grace oracles
Approve dedicated account, existing-session treatment, cleanup and independent recovery
Review boundary/timeout evidence and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

The missing half cannot be inferred from immediate session closure.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Functionality row 2254 Wistron-BMC Sanity-00036-V001: approve BMC/SSH build and authoritative MaxSess/SessTimeOut values and scope (per account/source/protocol/global, including existing/control sessions); define admission stage, boundary-plus-one rejection and concurrency settling; define true-idle/keepalive behavior, timeout start/maximum/grace and server-side close oracle; approve dedicated account, cleanup, resource aborts and independent recovery, and decide whether timeout is added here or separately scoped.

review_improvement: Preserves the six-session source scenario while restoring the omitted SessTimeOut coverage and preventing a resource fault or immediate cleanup from being mistaken for policy compliance.
independent_technical_reasoning: Session capacity and idle timeout are distinct controls. Capacity must count the correct protocol/account/global scope and distinguish TCP, authentication and shell acceptance; timeout requires an established session with no activity, while SSH keepalives may reset or mask the server timer. Existing sessions and the recovery channel can shift the boundary. Thus two explicitly measured checkpoints are required, and the original six-window-only procedure is a source conflict for the timeout half rather than evidence it passed.
